report.title: The other-day held-out sessions of CAN 11, 12 and 21 (2026-11-07 UTC)
report.question: On another day than their training (2026-11-07 UTC), do CAN 11, 12 and 21 still track and stop as they did, and does each twin of record still twin them?
report.note: CAN 12's session ran first (01:36 UTC); CAN 11's and CAN 21's first attempts were refused at preflight and ran again (r2, 03:28-03:34 UTC) after their frames were moved back by whole turns in RAM (bam_ws claude/otherday-rereference-1107, PEP 0016). Compare with ident-sessions-1106, the same stations' same-day held-out sessions.

models.name: twin
models.title: Rack twin: + cogging, delay, backlash, drive and heat (today's model)
models.equation: J q̈ = τ_motor(τ_cmd, delay, current loop, scale) − τ_r(q, q̇) − G sin(q − q_bottom); τ_r = friction level(v) sign(v) + b v + ripple(r q)

references.title: Jahns, Soong (1996). Pulsating torque minimization techniques for permanent magnet AC motor drives—a review. IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics.
references.note: cogging and commutation ripple as rotor harmonics

references.title: Nordin, Gutman (2002). Controlling mechanical systems with backlash—a survey. Automatica.
references.note: dead-zone backlash between motor and load

references.title: Tuttle, Seering (1996). A nonlinear model of a harmonic drive gear transmission. IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation.
references.note: a gear's compliance, friction and kinematic error

references.title: Krishnan (2010). Permanent Magnet Synchronous and Brushless DC Motor Drives. CRC Press.
references.note: field-oriented current loops of PM drives

needs.note: visited once: the type's coverage gate; physics extrapolates between cells

models.note: the drive's terms (torque scale, current loop, delay) are the board's: robotparts keeps them as the backend's driver, never a rung term
